snippet.title: Harry Potter Actors' LEAST Favorite Scenes To Film
snippet.description:
While living at Hogwarts and soaring through the air on flying broomsticks might seem like the most exciting and memorable experiences, the truth is the actors on the Harry Potter film sets didn’t always have such a great experience bringing magic to the screen. 

Ron actor had to face his real life fear - spiders! Like his character, Grant suffers arachnophobia. The underwater scenes look cool on screen - both figuratively AND literally. When filming during some of the coldest months of the year, the actors often found themselves freezing in water, feeling absolutely miserable. Rupert Grint felt so unwell once, he thought his heart had stopped beating and Daniel Radcliffe dealt with two ear infections! Let’s be honest, we’ve all wanted to mount a flying broom and try our hand at Quidditch, but hearing from  those who’ve actually experienced the wizarding world sport changes how keen we are to try. The actors hated having to film those scenes as they all found themselves in lots of pain and winding up with “numb bums.” 
In the later films as the characters are growing up, the content gets a bit more mature and kissing becomes more common. The actors, who’d all known each other for years and had very family-like relationships with each other dreaded filming these kissing scenes. Instead of being romantic, they were usually just very awkward. Having a whole crowd of people watching and filming very up close probably didn’t help matters either. The Room of Requirement may be a brilliant saviour for the witches and wizards throughout the series, but filming in the room wasn’t the best for the actors. Some actors were left feeling hysterical from claustrophobia and others were overheating - yikes!

snippet.title: All Of The Harry Potter Professor's Bloopers
snippet.description:
Harry Potter is full of quirky characters just a stone's throw away from the main cast. While Harry, Ron and Hermione are all charming in their own way, today we thought we’d look at some underappreciated characters in the stories. The professors. The professors are all freaking amazing characters and the actors behind them are hilarious geniuses. Emma Thompson gave one of the most amazing improvised bits in all of improv history while Professor Umbridge was speaking. And Umbridge behind the scenes is played by one goofy Imelda Staunton who’s best buds with Maggie Smith. The two together are a charming pair. Maggie once threatened to whack a student with a scroll. Of course, she didn’t mean it but it was funny. Maggie’s Professor McGonagall taught Ron to dance and Rupert insisted nobody ever breathe a word of the situation. Once, he doodled a picture of Alan Rickman and Rickman’s response might surprise you since we’re all so used to serious Severus Snape. He was such a genuine and kind guy who loved to laugh, especially with Michael Gambon. Michael and Alan played the most amazing prank on Daniel Radcliffe once. And once, while Radcliffe was hanging out in the side-car of Hagrid’s motorcycle, Robbie Coltrane started goofing around and made everyone on set giggle. Coltrane also celebrated over the thousandth take of a scene and somebody has yet to tell him that’s not a good thing. Warwick Davis went crowd surfing but that wasn’t the original plan. Richard Harris might have mistaken one of the animatronics for a real animal and the other Dumbledore had a knack for making Radcliffe laugh. While Miriam Margolyes, aka Professor Sprout, traumatized him.

snippet.title: Harry Potter Actors Who Injured Their Co-Stars While Filming
snippet.description:
Filming can be dangerous business, especially when in the magical and mystical world of Harry Potter. Actors often wound up accidentally injuring each other while in the midst of intense action - never on purpose of course, but some of these accidents were rough! 
Helena Bonham Carter nearly caused Matthew Lewis to go deaf after getting a bit too friendly with a wand - she did end up drawing blood and perforating his eardrum! Emma Watson caused a fair amount of pain to a few of her male colleagues whether she was feeling feisty and in the moment or she was taking a co-stars request a little too seriously - either way, it was a rough day for those actors she hurt!  While we know Lucius Malfoy is generally evil, Jason Isaacs actually stabbed Tom Felton once on set early on in the franchise! Talk about tough parenting. 
When Alan Rockman was on set, it was hard to tell whether he was being himself or Snape and this terrified the children - with good reason! Unfortunately, after the Snape actor had warned the young performers to be careful around his cloak, one young Hogwarts student messed up, accidentally causing injury to Rickman and earning a place in his bad books. 
It’s not just actors that caused issues - the set and props caused their fair share of damage, giving actors allergic reactions, freezing the soles of feet, causing headaches, and putting them in precarious situations.
No matter the situation, the actors braved through and managed to make it to the end of filming fairly unharmed!

snippet.title: Emma Watson and Rupert Grint interview
snippet.description:
This interview with Emma Watson and Rupert Grint was filmed shortly after the first film in the Harry Potter franchise had premiered in 2001 - Harry Potter and the Philosopher´s Stone. 

For all Americans  wondering why I wrote "Philosopher's Stone" and not "Sorcerer's stone":
"Philospher's stone" = The original, British title. 
"Sorcerer's stone" = The American title. 
The title change was proposed by J. K. Rowlings American publisher,  since they were concerned that Americans would not understand what a Philosopher is, given that it isn't the same in American English. This has, however, led to criticism as some argue that the title change might have been insulting to Americans. 
Rowling initially opposed the idea.

snippet.title: Harry Potter Auditions And How The Cast Landed The Role
snippet.description:
Behind The Scenes Of Harry Potter Cast Auditions As Child Stars 
Subscribe: http://bit.ly/Subscribe-to-Things

Hey Potterheads! Today on TheThings we’re taking a trip back to the year 2000 when the casting for Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone first kicked off. It’s hard to believe it’s been more than two decades since the start of the franchise but even more difficult to believe that the Harry Potter cast we know and love was almost completely different. We’re not kidding! 

The Harry Potter actors have very unconventional casting stories, but we wouldn’t have it any other way. From chance meetings at the theatre to casting directors scouring London primary schools - it’s so interesting to hear these actor’s individuals stories. 

And a little startling to find out that some of the cast members weren’t the first choice for their roles. 

We’re pretty sure you’ll have a hard time believing how these actors got their roles - it’s wild. Did you know that the Phelps twins had no idea who they were cast as until the first day on set? Or that Tom Felton originally auditioned for two other roles before landing Draco Malfoy? 

We’ll be covering almost the entire cast from Daniel Radcliffe, Rupert Grint, and Emma Watson all the way to Alan Rickman, Tom Felton, and Helena Bonham Carter. 

The paths to getting the cast we see on our screens today may have been unconventional but we wouldn’t have it any other way. What audition story did you find the most interesting? Make sure to let us know in the comment section below. We’d love it if you gave this video a big thumbs up and hit that subscribe button. Thanks for watching!

snippet.title: Harry Potter And The Deathly Hallows Part 2 Behind The Scenes
snippet.description:
What really went into the making of the final Harry Potter film? 

Hey, TheThings fans! Welcome back to another video. When Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 2 was released back in 2011 - it was the end of an era for not only Potterheads but for the cast and crew of this epic franchise. 

Being the last Harry Potter it’s no surprise that it’s one of the highest grossing Block Buster films ever. However, in order to make this possible, there was a lot of work that went into Harry Potter behind the scenes. Through special effects, cast bonds, and record-breaking moments, Deathly Hallows Part 2 is full of magic that can’t be seen without taking a journey behind the curtain and searching for the real wizardry. 

The golden trio’s Horcrux hunt comes to a peak in this film but so did the amount of effort from the cast and crew. They fought through emotional challenges, bone-chilling set locations, and mishaps with the law that had them having to recast a key character. 

This broom ride behind the scenes will have you looking at this film in a way you never have before. 

Ready to find out why Emma Watson had to have a cast of her bottom made for the final film? 

Without all these aspects coming together, especially between Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, and Ruper Grint, these movies - especially the finale - would never have been possible. If there’s any film that should be highlighted for team effort it’s Deathly Hallows Part 2. What do you think was the most epic behind-the-scenes moment? Let us know in the comment section below. Thanks for watching!
